clue.text: Meet cyclists at first at side of road

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word cyclists

parts.note: to be at a place is to be on it
a verge is the grassy strip along the side of a road

explanation.surface: Advice on where to gather for riders arriving first at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge come together, which is what meeting is.

clue.text: Whip used by largely merciless member of medieval sect

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: largely drops the final letter of the merciless word

parts.note: hard means harsh or merciless

explanation.surface: A whip wielded by a ruthless follower of a heretical medieval movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cathars were a dualist Christian sect in medieval southern France.

clue.text: Rules in court, most ignored quite regularly

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored, so the even ones of the three words remain

explanation.surface: Court rules are mostly disregarded as a matter of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are standards or rules of behaviour.

clue.text: Raised a flag after capturing rebel leaders in African country

indicators.note: capturing puts the rebel letters inside the raised pair
in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire
the leading two letters of the word rebel

explanation.surface: A flag is hoisted after rebel chiefs are seized in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb, TIRE. 'Raised' reverses A and TIRE to ERITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country on the Red Sea coast of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Danger —- Britain under attack! Keep stiff upper lip

indicators.note: under attack shows the letters being knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A wartime warning that Britain is threatened, urging calm resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a stiff upper lip is the idiom for enduring trouble without complaint.

clue.text: Believe this is a decent exam grade

definitions.meaning: to give credence to, accept as true
a pass with merit, above an ordinary pass in some marking schemes

explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe it, and a credit is a good grade in some exams.

clue.text: The first to retire to the country don't speak the language

indicators.note: The first to asks for only the opening letter of retire

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: The first to retreat to the countryside is told to stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Romansh is a Romance language spoken in Switzerland.

clue.text: Theatre producer not quite ready to wear women's clothing

indicators.note: a wearer is inside the clothes, so the ready word goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man

indicators.note: not quite drops the last letter

parts.note: mature means ripe or ready

explanation.surface: A stage producer, not fully prepared, is dressing up in female attire.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturg is a literary adviser in a theatre company, helping shape productions.

clue.text: One attempting to embrace me, last to wait in line

indicators.note: to embrace puts the following pieces inside the attempting word

parts.note: a trier is one who tries

indicators.note: last to takes the final letter of wait

explanation.surface: Someone trying to hug me, last to stand in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In line' suggests a queue, but 'line' is a line of verse; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimeter is a line of verse of three metrical feet.

clue.text: One putting the frighteners on soldier out of condition

indicators.note: the soldier stands outside the condition word, so it sits within him

parts.note: a terrier is slang for a member of Britain's Territorial Army
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Someone scaring others is a soldier who has let himself go physically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of condition' reads as unfit, but the soldier is placed out of, that is around, IF. A terrier is a Territorial Army volunteer, Britain's reserve soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifier is someone who frightens people, and putting the frighteners on someone is British slang for scaring them.

clue.text: Protest about Tommy's initial allowance after battle

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the battle

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium

indicators.note: initial asks for the first letter of Tommy

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A soldier complains about his rations after fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the British private soldier, fitting the Mons setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstration is a forceful protest or objection.

clue.text: US city reveals plan to back fast road

indicators.note: to back means to run the plan word in reverse

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: An American city reveals a scheme to support an express road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway running north from London; its '1' is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city in Florida, in the United States.

clue.text: Original setting for Mozart opera, lacking loud tune? The reverse

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for loud is dropped from the opera

parts.note: Faust is an opera by Gounod
f (forte) is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: The reverse tells the solver to turn the tune word backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Asking where a Mozart opera was first set, and whether a tune was played softly instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mozart opera' looks like one phrase, but Mozart belongs to the definition and the opera is Faust. 'The reverse' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart was born in Salzburg, so Austria is where his life was first set.

clue.text: Locks lunatic inside? That's not natural

indicators.note: inside puts the lunatic word within the locks word

parts.note: locks of hair, as on a horse or lion, make a mane
mad means lunatic

explanation.surface: Hair that holds a madman within is hardly what nature intended.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manufactured by people is artificial rather than natural.

clue.text: Half hope, after entering employment, to get a pension

indicators.note: after places half of hope behind the entering word

parts.note: boarding a ship or bus means entering it

indicators.note: Half asks for the first two of the four letters of hope

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: Hoping, once in work, to secure a retirement income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' looks like retirement pay; it is the French and European word for a guest house.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension in continental Europe is a modest boarding house serving lodgers.

clue.text: Supporters suppressing bad language, mostly, in sporting events

indicators.note: suppressing holds the bad language down inside the supporters

parts.note: braces support trousers

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: an oath is a swear word

explanation.surface: Fans keep their swearing in check, mostly, at sports fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' looks like fans; they are BRACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Boat races are rowing competitions, sporting events on water.

clue.text: Stupid dope involved in military takeover gets imprisoned

indicators.note: involved in puts the scrambled word within the takeover

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power by the army

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are in a muddle

explanation.surface: A foolish idiot caught up in a coup ends up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooped up means confined in a small space, as if in a chicken coop.

clue.text: Constrained by tight budget, old architect's forced to resign

parts.note: John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion

indicators.note: forced shows the words are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly architect is pushed into quitting his post.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on a shoestring is an idiom for managing with very little money.

clue.text: Spanish fellow so glad I had picked up cases

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, read upwards
cases means the words encase the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is happy to have collected some luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as fetched and 'cases' as luggage; together they turn OGLADIH, inside 'so glad I had', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the minor Spanish nobility, a gentleman.

clue.text: One English workers' group's supporting police force

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means placed below the police letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is military police
TU is a trade union, plus S from the possessive

explanation.surface: A single English union backs the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force that drives something forward.

clue.text: Group of pupils stumped right at start of test? That's not unknown

indicators.note: at start of sets these letters before the test word

parts.note: st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: not removes the unknown from the test word

parts.note: an exam is a test
x is the mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Pupils confused right from the start of an exam, though not clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumped is a cricket dismissal, written st. 'Not' drops X from EXAM, leaving EAM.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability taught together.

clue.text: Spanish hotel staff about to meet one coming by plane?

indicators.note: to meet sets the staff word beside the paratrooper

parts.note: a para, a paratrooper, arrives by jumping from an aircraft

indicators.note: about means the staff word is turned round

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Hotel employees going out to greet an arriving air passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' pretends to be hotel employees; it is a stick, ROD, reversed to DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A parador is one of Spain's state-run hotels, often in historic buildings.

clue.text: What you see on roads, eg signs for Car Park and Stop

parts.note: as means for example, as in fruits such as apples
a road sign for parking shows the letter P
halt means stop

explanation.surface: A list of road signs you might notice while driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarmac surface laid on roads.

clue.text: American/British affair

parts.note: our here is the British spelling ending, as in colour, where American has -or

explanation.surface: A transatlantic romance between an American and a Briton.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash suggests two nationalities, but British points to the -our spelling Britain uses for words like honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: Claude's endlessly drunk as a lord?

indicators.note: drunk shows the letters stagger into a new order
endlessly removes the final letter of the name

parts.note: the name Claude, its possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Claude has been drinking non-stop and is as drunk as a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'drunk as a lord' is split: 'drunk' signals the anagram and 'as a lord?' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to a duke, a noble lord; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Figure in the Tory reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges the members, here the letters

explanation.surface: A number of ministers caught up in a Conservative cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty-one is a number, and a figure is a number.

clue.text: Old shepherd taking step towards peak

parts.note: pas is a step in ballet
a tor is a rocky peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An elderly shepherd heads uphill towards a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: pastor is Latin for shepherd, an older sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastor originally meant a herdsman, the word later used for a spiritual shepherd of a congregation.

clue.text: Memory's a big worry at first for physicist

indicators.note: at first puts the worry ahead of the memory

parts.note: angst is deep anxiety
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A scientist's recollections are dominated by anxiety at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Ångström was a Swedish physicist after whom the unit of length is named.
